content.value_statement: Teams need clear architecture rules when codebases grow and design choices become inconsistent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical prompts for Clean Architecture, SOLID, DDD, and maintainability reviews.
actual_capabilities: Explains SOLID principles with responsibility and interface examples.
Maps Clean Architecture layers and dependency direction.
Encourages early returns, smaller functions, and domain-specific names.
Provides a checklist for architecture decisions before new code is written.
Identifies common anti-patterns such as God Class, deep nesting, and mixed concerns.
limitations: Does not inspect repositories by itself; the user must provide files or context.
Does not replace security, performance, or compliance reviews.
Examples are brief and mainly focused on TypeScript-style code.
Does not provide framework-specific implementation details for every stack.

use_cases.title: Review service boundaries
use_cases.description: Find mixed responsibilities, unclear dependencies, and weak domain naming before a service grows larger.

use_cases.title: Plan refactoring work
use_cases.description: Turn architecture smells into smaller steps that separate domain, application, infrastructure, and presentation concerns.

use_cases.title: Teach team standards
use_cases.description: Create shared guidance for SOLID, Clean Architecture, early returns, and library-first decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the software-architecture skill to explain Clean Architecture layers for my web app in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Review a component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the component I paste next. Identify SOLID issues, mixed concerns, and clearer domain names.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a refactor plan for this service. Separate domain, application, infrastructure, and presentation responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Define architecture standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate our architecture rules. Compare them against SOLID, Clean Architecture, DDD naming, and library-first decisions.

output_examples.input: Review this order module for architecture issues.
output_examples.output: A concise review listing mixed responsibilities, dependency direction issues, and clearer service boundaries.

output_examples.input: Design layers for a new billing feature.
output_examples.output: A layer map covering domain entities, use cases, adapters, infrastructure, and presentation responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Improve a deeply nested authorization flow.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for early returns, smaller policy methods, clearer names, and testable boundaries.

best_practices: Provide module purpose, current dependencies, and business rules before asking for an architecture review.
Ask for tradeoffs when choosing between a library, framework feature, or custom implementation.
Use the decision checklist before adding new layers or abstractions.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for broad architecture advice without describing the domain and constraints.
Do not use the skill as the only review for security-sensitive changes.
Do not add abstractions only to match a pattern name.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps review and plan software structure using Clean Architecture, SOLID, DDD naming, and maintainability checks.

faq.question: Can it review real code?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide code or file context for Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to inspect.

faq.question: Does it make architecture decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured guidance and tradeoffs so engineers can make informed decisions.

faq.question: Is it limited to TypeScript?
faq.answer: No. The examples use TypeScript style, but the architecture principles apply across languages.

faq.question: Can it replace a senior architecture review?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a checklist and review aid, not as final approval for high-risk systems.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the domain goal, current modules, key dependencies, constraints, and the change you want to make.
